Reading the table. Every row but one has at least three filled cells. The three worst cases:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Signatures} are written in nine kinds of place. A unit such as the bus phase has four specifications: the hole table (\texttt{protocol-\allowbreak{}blueprint.\allowbreak{}md:\allowbreak{}606}), the Layer 6 sketch (\texttt{:\allowbreak{}949-\allowbreak{}979}), the hole comment (\texttt{issue-\allowbreak{}12-\allowbreak{}comment-\allowbreak{}5833669972.\allowbreak{}md:\allowbreak{}61-\allowbreak{}73}) and the checklist line (\texttt{issue-\allowbreak{}12-\allowbreak{}body.\allowbreak{}md:\allowbreak{}30}). \Cref{sec:docs-contradictions} shows that they give three different types for it.
\item \textbf{The upstream ledger} is written three times, with different columns and different rows. The blueprint's has nine rows about ArkLib and a column ``Action'' (\texttt{protocol-\allowbreak{}blueprint.\allowbreak{}md:\allowbreak{}257-\allowbreak{}267}). The status's and the tracker's have twelve rows: they drop the context-lifting row and add four about Clean and leanISA (\texttt{protocol-\allowbreak{}status.\allowbreak{}md:\allowbreak{}171-\allowbreak{}184}, \texttt{issue-\allowbreak{}12-\allowbreak{}body.\allowbreak{}md:\allowbreak{}61-\allowbreak{}74}). The column ``Needed by'' names layers in the blueprint and holes in the other two.
\item \textbf{The record of a review} is written four times: the handoff's disposition table, the status's survey record (\texttt{protocol-\allowbreak{}status.\allowbreak{}md:\allowbreak{}438-\allowbreak{}536}), the tracker body (\texttt{issue-\allowbreak{}12-\allowbreak{}body.\allowbreak{}md:\allowbreak{}14}), and one line of \texttt{docs/\allowbreak{}README.\allowbreak{}md:\allowbreak{}38-\allowbreak{}47}.
\end{itemize}

Facts that exist only on the tracker, against the tracker's own claim to hold nothing of its own: the tests of nine units (\texttt{issue-\allowbreak{}12-\allowbreak{}comment-\allowbreak{}5833669972.\allowbreak{}md:\allowbreak{}38,\allowbreak{} 71,\allowbreak{} 85,\allowbreak{} 97,\allowbreak{} 125,\allowbreak{} 152,\allowbreak{} 166,\allowbreak{} 180,\allowbreak{} 194}), for example ``\texttt{blake2sBytes} on the RFC 7693 test vector'' (\texttt{:\allowbreak{}166}) and ``every pinned coding parameter with an achievability witness'' (\texttt{:\allowbreak{}152}); the remark that leanVM's chain is Merkle-Damgård and not a duplex sponge, ``so the transfer theorem, not the sponge, is what applies'' (\texttt{:\allowbreak{}182}); the review order of the open pull requests (\texttt{issue-\allowbreak{}12-\allowbreak{}body.\allowbreak{}md:\allowbreak{}48-\allowbreak{}57}); and what the spine asks of the Flock roadmap, which is a comment on issue 3 (id 5872015596).
